name: Sable Noir Ube-Black Sesame Tablets
description: Thin, breakable tablets made from Sable Noir's proprietary cacao-analog compound blended with ube extract and roasted black sesame paste. The snap and melt are engineered to mimic real chocolate within measurable tolerances.
flavor_profile: Deep, slightly bitter cacao-analog base; sweet purple ube earthiness mid-palate; roasted black sesame adds a nutty, smoky finish; the melt is slow and rich for a synth product
cultural_context: Sable Noir occupies an uncomfortable market position — premium enough to feel like a treat for Tier 3, but obviously not real chocolate. Tier 4 buyers purchase it for casual consumption while saving real cocoa for occasions. The brand never claims to be real chocolate, which has become a kind of honesty people respect.
story_hooks: A Sable Noir executive has obtained a small supply of actual cacao and is secretly blending it into one SKU without updating labeling — a food fraud case waiting to happen
A Tier 3 food critic's review claiming Sable Noir 'exceeds real chocolate' has gone viral and sparked furious debate about whether real ingredients still matter
Someone is selling counterfeit Sable Noir tablets filled with a mood-modulating compound — buyers think they're getting a treat; they're getting dosed
